narrative.intro: Brasfield and Gorrie has $416M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date, from 16 awards with an average award size of $26M, and obligations are down 5.8% year over year. Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, accounting for $326M of obligations, followed by Department of Defense with $59.6M and General Services Administration with $21.1M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the dominant market, accounting for $416M in obligations; smaller obligations appear in Engineering Services ($200K) and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction ($10K). Historical fiscal-year obligations show wide variation: FY21 was $178M, FY22 was $154M, FY23 was $679M, FY24 was $587M, FY25 was $442M, and FY26 is $416M to date. All figures are contract obligations except where award-value totals are explicitly noted as total contract values. This snapshot shows where Brasfield and Gorrie’s federal revenue is concentrated and how current-year totals compare to recent fiscal years.

sections.heading: Who are the top federal buyers of Brasfield and Gorrie in FY2026 to date?
sections.body: Department of Homeland Security is Brasfield and Gorrie’s largest federal customer with $326M in obligations. Department of Defense follows with $59.6M, and General Services Administration follows with $21.1M. Brasfield and Gorrie also received $9.8M from the Department of Justice and $200K from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

sections.heading: What markets and contract sizes define Brasfield and Gorrie’s federal work?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is Brasfield and Gorrie’s primary market with $416M in obligations. Brasfield and Gorrie has $200K in Engineering Services and $10K in Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction. Brasfield and Gorrie’s average award size in FY2026 to date is $26M across 16 awards.

faq.q: How much does Brasfield and Gorrie make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Brasfield and Gorrie has $416M in contract obligations from federal work in FY2026 to date. Brasfield and Gorrie’s federal total comes from 16 awards with an average award size of $26M, and obligations are down 5.8% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Brasfield and Gorrie?
faq.a: Department of Homeland Security, Department of Defense, and General Services Administration are Brasfield and Gorrie’s top buyers. Brasfield and Gorrie received $326M from the Department of Homeland Security, $59.6M from the Department of Defense, $21.1M from the General Services Administration, $9.8M from the Department of Justice, and $200K from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

faq.q: What does Brasfield and Gorrie sell to the government?
faq.a: Brasfield and Gorrie primarily sells construction services to the federal government. Brasfield and Gorrie’s largest market is Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with $416M in obligations, with additional obligations in Engineering Services ($200K) and Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction ($10K).
